nodes.summary: Factor vision, temporal modeling and action selection into separate trainable components.
nodes.definition: World Models separates visual compression, temporal prediction and control. A variational autoencoder maps an image to a latent vector. A recurrent mixture-density model predicts future latent distributions conditioned on actions and memory. A compact controller uses these features to select actions. The experiments investigate whether policies can exploit a learned internal model, including training a Doom policy in a generated environment. This is a historically important learned-model design, rather than a claim that every task can be solved in an imagined environment.
nodes.example: For a racing image, first obtain a visual latent and update recurrent memory using the previous action. The controller outputs steering and acceleration from those features. In the separate Doom experiment, policy training occurs inside the learned model. These two protocols must not be merged into a single statement that all reported controllers were trained entirely in imagination.
nodes.role_en: This foundational example connects VAE representations, recurrent dynamics, uncertainty and controller learning. Its game experiments motivate robot modeling concepts, but are not themselves robot-hardware validation.

nodes.title: 从像素学习潜在动力学并规划
nodes.summary: Learn probabilistic latent dynamics for online planning directly from image observations.
nodes.definition: PlaNet learns image-based dynamics and selects actions through online planning in latent space. Its recurrent state-space model combines deterministic memory with stochastic state, allowing uncertainty and information from past observations to coexist. Image and reward reconstruction train the model, while latent overshooting encourages predictions over multiple time steps. At action selection, candidate sequences are evaluated in this learned state space. Unlike a direct policy that returns an action in one network call, PlaNet repeatedly uses trajectory optimization to choose a plan.
nodes.example: From a camera observation of a simulated walker, infer the current latent state. Sample candidate motor sequences, predict their latent trajectories and rewards, and retain promising sequences with CEM. Execute part of the best plan, obtain a new image and repeat. The decoder helps training but need not render every candidate image during planning.
nodes.role_en: PlaNet is a key bridge from probabilistic state-space modeling to learned visual MPC. Its RSSM and planning/acting distinction support understanding later imagination-based agents.

nodes.title: 通过潜在想象学习控制策略
nodes.summary: Learn behavior through latent imagination rather than only online action-sequence search.
nodes.definition: Dreamer learns a latent dynamics model from observations and then trains an actor and a value function using imagined trajectories. The actor can receive gradients through differentiable latent transitions, which helps optimize behavior over a longer effective horizon than directly searching a long raw action sequence. A learned value function supplies estimates beyond a finite imagined rollout. The distinction is structural: the world model is learned from experience, while the behavior is improved inside that model and then used to collect or execute real environment actions.
nodes.example: Infer a latent state from the current camera frame. Starting at that state, unroll several model transitions using the actor, predict rewards and bootstrap the remaining return with the value model. Update the actor using those imagined outcomes. At environment time, action selection uses the actor instead of rerunning a full CEM search for every decision.
nodes.role_en: Dreamer links backpropagation through time, latent probabilistic modeling and actor-critic training. It provides a useful contrast to ID-WM, which searches for goal-reaching decisions at inference.

nodes.summary: Use discrete stochastic states and training stabilization to extend imagination-based learning to Atari.
nodes.definition: DreamerV2 develops the Dreamer recipe using categorical latent variables and stabilized world-model and behavior learning. Stochastic latent categories are sampled while straight-through gradients provide an approximate differentiable path. KL balancing separates the pressure applied to prior and posterior distributions. The model learns from environment experience and trains behavior through imagined states. Its Atari results establish a particular sample-efficient game-learning capability; they do not automatically imply accurate continuous robot contact dynamics or unrestricted transfer to other embodiments.
nodes.example: An image encoder infers categorical latent state from an Atari frame. The prior predicts the next distribution without seeing the future image; the posterior uses the next image during training. KL-related losses align them. An actor learns from rollouts under the prior, so prior errors matter even if posterior reconstructions look accurate.
nodes.role_en: This paper connects categorical random variables, approximate gradients and probabilistic model training. It clarifies why latent distribution design is a separate architectural choice from action or policy representation.

nodes.summary: Stabilize the Dreamer learning system for broad task diversity with a shared recipe.
nodes.definition: DreamerV3 targets an imagination-based reinforcement-learning algorithm that remains effective across diverse observation spaces, action types and reward scales. It retains the recurrent stochastic world model, actor and critic, while introducing normalization and prediction choices such as symlog transforms, distributional targets and balanced regularization. These changes reduce per-domain retuning in the reported evaluation. The work should be understood as a robust training system whose components interact, not as a single new dynamics-layer architecture or a universal proof of generalization.
nodes.example: Consider one task with tiny rewards and another with much larger returns. A fixed raw regression loss can put them on incompatible numerical scales. DreamerV3 transforms targets and normalizes behavior-learning signals so the same algorithm settings can be tested more broadly. Performance still depends on training interaction, task construction and model capacity.
nodes.role_en: This is the modern Dreamer-family reference for stable model-based RL. It connects numerical scaling and distributional prediction to practical training, including robotics-like continuous-control benchmarks.

nodes.title: 时序差分学习与模型预测控制
nodes.summary: Combine local model-based optimization and temporal-difference terminal values.
nodes.definition: TD-MPC combines short-horizon latent trajectory optimization with a learned terminal value estimate. Its task-oriented latent dynamics model is trained jointly with reward and value components, rather than being required to reconstruct every image detail. The planner uses local modeled rewards and the terminal value to evaluate candidate action sequences. Temporal-difference learning supplies long-range reward information. This differs from reward-free goal-distance planning: the latent space is shaped by the task and its return-prediction objective.
nodes.example: For a reaching task, compare several short motor sequences using predicted rewards. At the end of each short rollout, add the learned value of the predicted terminal state. A sequence that is initially indirect can still score well if its terminal value predicts future progress beyond the rollout horizon.
nodes.role_en: TD-MPC illustrates how value learning compensates for limited model horizon. It is an important comparison branch for understanding what ID-WM gains or avoids by using goal-driven subgoals instead of task values.

nodes.summary: Scale and stabilize latent MPC across tasks, embodiments and model sizes.
nodes.definition: TD-MPC2 improves the TD-MPC learning and planning system for robustness across many continuous-control tasks. It keeps decoder-free latent dynamics and terminal-value-guided local optimization, while changing representation constraints, value-learning design and training stabilization. The work studies larger models and multi-task training with different embodiments and action spaces. Its reported shared-hyperparameter performance is evidence within a specified benchmark collection; it is not equivalent to a model that controls arbitrary unseen robots without data or calibration.
nodes.example: A multi-task training batch may contain trajectories from different control problems. Planning still uses the task context and admissible action dimensions, rather than interpreting all tasks as one identical action space.

nodes.title: 图像联合嵌入预测架构
nodes.summary: Predict semantic image-region embeddings from context without pixel reconstruction or negative pairs.
nodes.definition: I-JEPA learns image representations by predicting target-region features from visible context-region features. The target branch encodes the image and supplies stop-gradient representation targets; a predictor uses context and target-position information. Large target blocks and informative distributed context encourage semantic prediction rather than merely interpolating nearby pixel texture. The objective predicts representations rather than reconstructing pixels or contrasting against a set of negative examples. This is a representation-learning paper, not yet an action-conditioned robot dynamics model.
nodes.example: Hide several image blocks while leaving spatially distributed context visible. The context encoder and predictor estimate the target encoder features at the hidden positions. Matching these vectors trains useful image features. No robot action enters this image-only training example, so a controller cannot obtain motor consequences merely by running the encoder.
nodes.role_en: I-JEPA provides the representation-prediction foundation for later video JEPAs and action-conditioned predictive models. It should remain distinct from the full control loop.

nodes.summary: Learn video representations using masked feature prediction alone.
nodes.definition: V-JEPA extends feature prediction to masked spatiotemporal regions in video. A context encoder sees visible video tokens; a predictor estimates target representations computed by a separate target encoder. Training does not require action labels, text, negative examples or pixel reconstruction. The resulting representation is evaluated through downstream video and image tasks, including motion-sensitive recognition. Video representation learning can support later world modeling, but this action-free objective should not be presented as an executable robot controller or an explicit action-conditioned simulator.
nodes.example: Take a short video of an object moving across a table and mask blocks across space and time. The model predicts features at those positions from the remaining clip. It can learn motion-related structure without producing the missing RGB frames. Predicting features from a partially visible clip is also not identical to always predicting strictly future frames.
nodes.role_en: This is the original video-JEPA paper, linking temporal tokenization, positional encoding and self-supervised target prediction. Action-conditioned planning is introduced in later extensions.

An exponential-moving-average target encoder instead defines how target parameters are updated over training iterations. nodes.summary: Use probabilistic model ensembles with trajectory sampling for sample-efficient continuous control.
nodes.definition: PETS learns an ensemble of probabilistic neural dynamics models and propagates their uncertainty with sampled trajectories during planning. Each model predicts a state-change distribution, while differences between members reflect uncertainty associated with limited training coverage. Candidate action sequences are evaluated using particles and sampling-based optimization in an MPC loop. The method explicitly studies uncertainty-aware planning rather than treating a single deterministic model prediction as certain. Ensemble disagreement is useful but is not automatically a calibrated probability of failure on every unseen state.
nodes.example: For each candidate action sequence, propagate several state particles while sampling ensemble members and transition noise according to the chosen trajectory-sampling variant. Compare predicted returns across these particles, refine candidates with CEM and execute the first action. When models disagree about an unfamiliar contact state, the planner sees a broader outcome distribution than a single mean prediction would provide.
nodes.role_en: PETS connects probabilistic regression, epistemic versus aleatoric uncertainty, ensembles and MPC. It is a practical state-space model-based control foundation that complements representation-focused world-model papers.

Candidate action sequences are evaluated using particles and sampling-based optimization in an MPC loop. The method explicitly studies uncertainty-aware planning rather than treating a single deterministic model prediction as certain. Ensemble disagreement is useful but is not automatically a calibrated probability of failure on every unseen state.

nodes.summary: Use short model-generated rollouts branched from real data to balance sample reuse against model bias.
nodes.definition: MBPO studies how much to use a learned dynamics model when improving a policy. Its practical algorithm starts short synthetic rollouts from states sampled from real replay, then mixes generated transitions with real data for off-policy actor-critic updates. This separates modeling from behavior optimization and reduces reliance on long open-loop imagined trajectories. The theoretical analysis motivates the tradeoff between additional synthetic experience and model bias; its monotonic-improvement analysis should not be treated as an unconditional guarantee for an arbitrary learned neural simulator.
nodes.example: Choose a state from a real replay buffer, run the current policy through the learned ensemble for only a few steps, and store those imagined transitions separately. Use many such short branches to train the policy. Restarting from recorded states limits the distance traveled through a potentially inaccurate model, although distribution shift can still occur within each branch.
nodes.role_en: MBPO explains why longer model rollouts are not always better. It connects learned dynamics to off-policy optimization and provides a useful comparison with latent imagination agents that use different state and gradient pathways.

nodes.summary: Learn visual interaction simulation from diverse datasets and use it to train embodied policies.
nodes.definition: UniSim learns a generative visual simulator of interactions by combining datasets that contribute different forms of coverage: diverse objects, camera motion, human behavior or robot actions. The model can be conditioned on high-level language or low-level action descriptions to generate visual outcomes. The paper explores using simulated experience to train high-level and low-level policies and evaluates selected transfers to the real world. Its universal-simulator framing is an objective for broad interaction modeling, not a demonstrated replacement for every physical simulation subsystem.
nodes.example: An image dataset can supply object diversity while a robot dataset supplies action-conditioned movement examples. Train one conditional generator on the combined interfaces, then request a future showing a drawer opening from a current view. A policy trained using these generated interactions must still be tested on the relevant hardware and task; visual plausibility alone cannot establish the accuracy of hidden forces.
nodes.role_en: UniSim is an important bridge from general video generation to robot-policy training through learned interaction simulation. It motivates separate evaluation of visual quality, action controllability and real policy transfer.

nodes.summary: Use language-conditioned video plans as a shared planning interface, then ground them into task-specific actions.
nodes.definition: UniPi formulates a policy through a text-conditioned video plan and a separate action-grounding mechanism. The generator is explicitly conditioned on the starting observation, and temporal super-resolution refines sparse coarse plans into more detailed sequences. A task-specific inverse-dynamics adapter translates visual transitions into executable actions. This separation allows video and language data to contribute planning knowledge across environments, while the action interface still needs environment-specific data. A compelling robot video plan should not be confused with demonstrated physical execution of that plan.
nodes.example: Provide an image and the goal to place an object left of another object. Generate sparse intermediate frames, refine them in time and infer control actions with an adapter trained for the target environment. Execute with observation feedback. The same visual planner can propose plans for different environments, but a control mapping from one robot cannot automatically be sent to another embodiment.

nodes.summary: Combine causal sequence prediction and diffusion by independently corrupting token positions.
nodes.definition: Diffusion Forcing trains a causal sequence model to denoise tokens whose noise levels are sampled independently across the sequence. This permits observed history and uncertain future positions to have different corruption levels, combining variable-length autoregressive generation with diffusion-style guidance. At sampling time, different causal noise schedules support robust rollout and planning. The framework is broader than one robot policy architecture: the paper evaluates video prediction, decision-making, robot-related tasks and time-series settings under distinct configurations. Long generation alone does not establish long-horizon physical accuracy.
nodes.example: Keep past observations near the clean end of the diffusion schedule while initializing future tokens with stronger noise. Denoise future positions conditionally, without requiring every past token to be fully corrupted again. Guidance can favor desirable trajectories. Training with independent noise levels teaches the model to handle many combinations of reliable and uncertain token positions.
nodes.role_en: This paper bridges next-token prediction, full-sequence diffusion, causal conditioning and guidance-based planning. It is useful for understanding flexible-horizon world models without treating every diffusion sampler as an identical temporal model.
